public_rationale: The contextual warning against general reliance without checking is supported. September testing found very low completion rates for leading models on complex commercial coding tasks, directly relevant to the post's examples. GDPval also showed useful, competitive professional work, so the evidence does not support the stronger claim that every task or use is unreliable. This assessment depends on the stated ordinary reading.
limitations: The strongest outcome evidence concerns difficult software-engineering tasks.
Performance depends on the model, task, tools, and execution setup.
Successful assisted use is compatible with the supported warning.
The cited tests do not establish universal or repeated-run unreliability.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Large language models cannot be relied on to do what users want.

statement.excerpt: You cannot rely on a large language model to do what you want.

from_speaker: cannot rely on a large language model
can’t actually be relied upon to do exactly what you want
correctly, or even consistently, every time
our_interpretation: The ordinary contextual reading is that contemporary LLMs cannot generally be trusted to complete requested work correctly without checking, particularly complex or multistep work.
This does not mean that LLMs never succeed, that every task is unreliable, or that useful systems must be mathematically infallible.
Use September 2025 through publication as the latest contemporaneous observation window; there is no standardized reporting quarter for model reliability.
Assess models and configurations available then. Later improvements do not settle this historical observation.
criteria.support_condition: Contemporaneous evaluations show substantial failures to complete clear, realistic user tasks, including complex work emphasized in the context, sufficient to undermine general reliance without verification.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Broad, independently replicated evaluations establish consistently correct completion across representative routine and multistep user tasks without substantial human correction. Isolated successful demonstrations are insufficient.

evidence.locator: Results: SWE-Bench Verified vs. SWE-Bench Pro; private commercial subset
evidence.explanation: The September benchmark report found that leading models completed only a small minority of complex private-codebase tasks under the tested setup. This supports the warning against assuming correct autonomous completion of such work.

GDPval supplies a material qualification: models produced competitive work across professional tasks. Its expert-preference comparisons and one-shot design do not establish consistent correctness over repeated runs.
